topic: A day on Venus is longer than its year
mainFact: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun, so its day is longer than its year.
supportingDetails: Venus spins backwards compared to most planets, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
Venus is the hottest planet, with a surface around 475 degrees Celsius, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
caption: Would you survive one day on Venus? Most people get this wrong 👀

scenes.narration: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
scenes.headline: A day longer than a year?

scenes.narration: Here is why. Venus spins super slowly. One full spin takes about two hundred forty-three Earth days.
scenes.headline: Venus spins super slowly

scenes.narration: But its trip around the Sun is quicker. One full orbit takes only about two hundred twenty-five Earth days.
scenes.headline: One trip around the Sun

scenes.narration: So on Venus, one single day lasts longer than a whole year. Your birthday would come before tomorrow!
scenes.headline: The day beats the year

scenes.narration: And it gets even weirder. Venus spins backwards compared to Earth and most other planets.
scenes.headline: It spins backwards

visual.caption: Venus spins the opposite way to Earth

scenes.narration: That means on Venus, the Sun rises in the west and slowly sets in the east.
scenes.headline: Sunrise in the west

scenes.narration: Venus is also the hottest planet in our solar system, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
scenes.headline: The hottest planet

scenes.narration: Its thick clouds trap heat, so the ground reaches about four hundred seventy-five degrees Celsius. Hot enough to melt lead!
scenes.headline: Hot enough to melt lead

scenes.narration: Quick recap. Venus spins slowly and backwards, so its day is longer than its year.
scenes.headline: Quick recap

scenes.headline: A new fact every day!
